title: Comparing Systems You Can Trust: Samples, Variance and Significance
summary: A higher score on an eval set does not mean a better system. This lesson shows how to put error bars on pass rates, test whether a difference is real, exploit paired data, bootstrap anything, plan the sample size, and avoid fooling yourself with many comparisons.
objectives: Compute a standard error and 95% confidence interval for a pass rate
Run a two-proportion z-test and interpret the p-value correctly
Use a paired comparison and McNemar's test when both systems answer the same items
Build a bootstrap confidence interval for any metric
Compute the sample size needed to detect a given improvement, and correct for multiple comparisons
prerequisites: The idea that an eval score is an average, and the standard error formula, from [Success Criteria](/learn/evaluation/success-criteria). Judge agreement from [Using a Model as a Judge](/learn/evaluation/llm-as-judge) is useful but not required.
